guidanceForV1_8.askedFor: The coordinator asks whether this re-binding changes what v1.8 should contain.
guidanceForV1_8.answer: YES, in four respects. The three repair sites are necessary and not sufficient.

items.what: Repair the reason, not only the number. The third site reads 'the longest text component across all seventeen vectors is 71 bytes, THE WIDTH OF A DIGEST.' Changing 71 to 79 and leaving 'the width of a Digest' reproduces the retention-tiers.v26 defect the freeze already records -- value corrected, prose left stale -- inside the repair for a defect of the same family. The longest component is now a derived findingId, not a Digest, and the sentence must say so.

Do not patch three rows; re-derive the class. The question that was never asked is 'what else in the predecessor was MEASURING the leaves I just changed?' Patching the three sites answers the instances. Re-deriving the class -- sweep every recorded measurement in the resolved contract whose REFERENT is a leaf any operation modifies, scoped by referent and with the row set derived rather than enumerated -- answers the property. I found three sites; I did not derive the class either, and I cannot certify that three is the whole of it.

79 is a DERIVED quantity, not a constant. It is 79 only because the prefix 'finding:' is 8 bytes and the digest text is 71. If v1.8 or any successor changes the prefix, the render or the hash width, the figure moves again and this exact defect recurs. Express it as derived from the findingId construction, or at minimum note the dependency next to the value.

Fold in A-7, A-1 and A-5 in the same pass -- they are one clause each and all three are in the same family of stale or missing provenance. A-7 in particular will otherwise re-fire on v1.8 immediately, because the freeze pin it would inherit is ALREADY stale at 010f9b11 against a live 6e0d36a6, and v1.7 dropped the driftDisclosure mechanism v1.6 used to handle exactly this.

Whatever v1.8 contains, it is a new byte state and neither the original verdict nor this addendum binds it. Freeze 7.2: a change to reviewed bytes requires a version bump and a NEW verdict. That is satisfied by v1.8 being a new file, and it requires a new review -- this addendum must not be read as pre-clearing the repair.
